dedupe_keys.name: u s space economy statistics bea

description: The U.S. space economy statistics of the Bureau of Economic Analysis measure the contribution of space-related industries to the U.S. economy: value added to gross domestic product, gross output by industry, and private employment and compensation by industry, with a list of the commodities counted as space goods and services. BEA, the federal statistical agency for national accounts, produced them as a satellite account to inform business leaders, policymakers and the public. Coverage is national for the United States, annual for 2012 to 2023, released on 31 March 2025. Format and access: XLSX tables and articles in the Survey of Current Business, free to download from the BEA page. Licence: U.S. federal statistics in the public domain. Caveats: BEA states that it will no longer regularly produce these statistics, so the series ends in 2023, and the space definition is BEA's, which differs from other measures. It serves capacity planning and economic dependence analysis of space infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the BEA input-output accounts on which the estimates are built, and the OECD-ESA-Eurostat classification work listed on the page.
